text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A27, A36, A37 and A42 appear in essentially every trace (about 995–1000 in 1000, up from about 46–55 in 100), and each occurs about once per trace where it previously occurred about half as often. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- In the later window, A25's outgoing transitions shifted from almost exclusively to A28 (about 97 in 100) to an even three-way split across A36, A37 and A42 (about 31–34 in 100 each), and A26's outgoing transitions shifted from a mixed split (A27 about 54 in 100, A36/A37/A42 together about 45 in 100) to A27 alone (about 98 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002]
- In the later window, A36, A37 and A42 each route onward to A28 (about 31–34 in 100 of their outgoing transitions) where they previously routed to A31 (about 29–39 in 100); direct transitions from these activities into A31 are no longer observed. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- In the later window the order around the A36/A37/A42 group reversed: the group now precedes A26 in about 98–99 in 100 co-occurrences (previously A26 always preceded it), now precedes A28 in about 97–99 in 100 (previously A28 preceded it), and now co-occurs with A27 in about 995 in 1000 traces with the group first (about 96–97 in 100), whereas before the group and A27 hardly ever shared a trace (about 1–2 in 100); A25 precedes each group member in about 97–99 in 100. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- In the later window A36, A37 and A42 occur together in about 995 in 1000 traces in varying internal order (about 47–51 in 100 in either direction), whereas before they co-occurred in about 46 in 100 traces and about 53 in 100 traces contained none of them. [REL020, REL021, REL022]
- Relative event positions moved accordingly: A36, A37 and A42 shifted earlier (mean position from about 0.59 to about 0.41 of the trace), while A26, A27 and A28 shifted later (about 0.54 to 0.60, 0.58 to 0.63, and 0.40 to 0.46). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Distances changed consistently: A28 now follows A25 by 4–5 steps (about 91 and 8 in 100 cases) where it immediately followed A25 before (gap of 1 in about 96 in 100), and the distance from A26 to A31 became consistently 2 steps (about 97 in 100) after being split between 2 and 4 steps. [LAG001, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

One possibility supported by the evidence is that the group formed by A36, A37 and A42 was repositioned: in the earlier window it ran in about 46 in 100 cases as an alternative to A27 after A26 and led into A31, while in the later window it runs in virtually every case after A25 and before A26, leads into A28, and A27 has become the near-exclusive successor of A26, with A28 now following the group rather than A25 directly; A31 remains in every trace and still follows both the group and A27. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL014, POS005]

- The order changes are observed directly, not inferred from frequencies alone: the direction between A26 and each of A36, A37, A42 reversed, and the direction between A28 and each of them reversed, in pairs where the anchor activities are present throughout. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- Routing, participation, position and distance indicators all line up with the same rearrangement, and the three group members behave as one unit (simultaneous participation gain, near-universal co-occurrence, mixed internal order). [DIR001, DIR002, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS006, POS007, POS008, REL020, REL021, REL022]
- With 48 qualifying items against roughly 0.74 expected for an unchanged process, the evidence set as a whole is unlikely to be a chance product, and each item's difference exceeds all but about 1 in 200 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, DIR001, REL006, REL011, LAG001]

Limitations: the windows are samples of 200 traces each, and variant frequencies can differ between such samples without any change; a jump from about 46 to about 995 in 1000 together with order reversals among ever-present activities makes pure sampling an unlikely explanation, but it cannot be fully excluded. [OCC002, REL006, REL014] Several distance items rest on only 1–2 observed pairs (for example the distances from A26 to A36, A37 and A42 in the later window) and were not relied upon; the distance conclusions use items backed by about 200 observations per window, and all positions and distances are measured in event order, not clock time. [LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006] Finally, a before/after comparison cannot distinguish a repositioning of the existing group from a removal of the old branch combined with an insertion of a similar group earlier in the process; what is established is the change in the relations themselves. [REL006, REL014, DIR003]
